author: m.kalinin
content: Now it's getting clearer to me. So, we have `N` blocks behind the most recent finalized checkpoint, for the period of non-finality this implies also retaining blocks up until the head after that checkpoint

author: m.kalinin
content: There were efforts on supporting the checkpoint sync from a non-finalized checkpoint in several clients, not sure about that status of this work. This is helpful for bootstrapping a node during long non-finality period or for switching a node to a desirable fork. Starting from a finalized checkpoint in this case may also work. If EL has been bootstrapped already and the restart happens with wiping out CL's database leaving EL with the state it has, then EL will be syncing by executing blocks from the point where it went offline and it will be helpful to have those blocks in the network, otherwise, EL will need to get wiped out and snap synced from scratch i guess

author: tersec
content: top-up sync

author: tersec
content: > If EL has been bootstrapped already and the restart happens with wiping out CL's database leaving EL with the state it has, then EL will be syncing by executing blocks from the point where it went offline and it will be helpful to have those blocks in the network, otherwise, EL will need to get wiped out and snap synced from scratch i guess

author: tersec
content: i.e. this is one advantage of having a method to treat the EL as a kind of library which doesn't itself need to gossip

author: m.kalinin
content: top-up sync relies on blocks requested over p2p, right? So, beacon blocks and payloads should be available since the point in time when node went offline

author: tersec
content: well they need to be available somehow to the _CL_. But not the EL

author: m.kalinin
content: I see, and some CL clients offload payloads and request them from EL

author: m.kalinin
content: and when you bootstrap a nimbus node from scratch, its EL will have to rely on the snap sync, right? It doesn't use top-up sync for syncing from scratch

author: m.kalinin
content: I am asking because in theory it could do, could use a trusted EL state to top-up sync from

author: tersec
content: Yeah, I don't see how it can avoid that currently, unless the CL feeds it blocks all the way from genesis, which seems infeasible/too slow

author: tersec
content: but that gap between a somewhat-recent state and head can be filled

author: tersec
content: where somewhat-recent is any time within the CL's block retention period

author: m.kalinin
content: i see, thank for clarification!

author: yorickdowne
content: Is rolling expiry in Nethermind still experimental?

author: svlachakis
content: It's not experimental, we have full support for EraE we just haven't merged the change for the defaults yet - just waiting for more clients to align. <@543900561460822016> confirmed geth is good with this limit

author: yorickdowne
content: Thanks! I still had it marked as experimental because of v1.33.0 release notes ("It is an experimental feature, not yet recommended for use on production nodes.") and not having seen it elevated to production in release notes since.

author: svlachakis
content: This statement was only in release notes and will mention it explicitly together with changing the defaults, but is fully functional already. It was just a matter of first release of the feature, it's end to end tested.

author: svlachakis
content: Do you have any specifc use case in mind for the feature?

author: yorickdowne
content:
I am offering it in Eth Docker. I'll be changing the default to `33_024` when users choose `rolling-expiry`, once that's in a Nethermind release.

This is useful for solo stakers, or those using Eth Docker for Lido CSM or RocketPool. SSV and NodeSet will need to stick with `pre-merge-expiry` because they need post-merge receipts.

author: yorickdowne
content: Ethrex is working on expiry as well afaik. With Geth (and maybe Ethrex) adding rolling expiry, it'll be in all clients. Still experimental in Besu. And that allows me to then also add it to the `config` workflow in a future step. Right now config queries for pre-merge expiry. After clients all have rolling for `33_024` epochs as an option, I'll query accordingly unless a user is running RPC (presumably full node), or SSV (needs post-merge receipts)

author: yorickdowne
content: People with 2TB disks are starting to get nervous again with pre-merge expiry, as seen in the EthCoordinate and RocketPool support Discords. Rolling expiry is coming at the right time.

author: svlachakis
content:
Quick check on what you want Eth Docker to set ideally: for the rolling-expiry option, are you planning to enable `History.Pruning=Rolling` (which also prunes already-synced nodes and is what actually frees disk for your 2TB users), or only cap what a fresh sync downloads via the ancient barriers?

Asking because the pruning path already works on current releases at `History.RetentionEpochs=82125`; the only thing `33_024` specifically needs is the lower floor that is about to land. The barrier defaults we are changing only affect fresh syncs, so on their own they do nothing for a node that is already synced.

author: yorickdowne
content: I currently use `History.Pruning=Rolling` and will continue to do so, just with a new retentionepochs

author: yorickdowne
content: RocketPool just did the same in their latest release, they also use `History.Pruning=Rolling`. They could decide to adjust RetentionEpochs in future, as well.
